fatal_errors: The proposed aluminum/ECAP system is unrelated to the target comparison between NbMoTaW and Re-containing NbMoTaWRe refractory high-entropy-alloy films.
It omits helium implantation, irradiation-induced hardening, helium-bubble segregation, and grain-boundary embrittlement, which define the target problem.

The assertion that four-pass ECAP aluminum will be more ductile than annealed aluminum is unsupported and not generally reliable; severe grain refinement commonly raises strength while reducing uniform elongation relative to a fully annealed state.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses ductility only in a broad sense and reconstructs none of the target material, intervention, irradiation conditions, mechanism, baseline, or outcomes. Its proposed tensile comparison could test its own aluminum claim, but it would not discriminate the target finding that Re addition improves the helium-irradiation resistance of sputtered NbMoTaW-based films. The mechanism also conflates ultrafine-grain strengthening, dislocation motion, and grain-boundary sliding without establishing that these processes increase room-temperature tensile ductility.
